nodes.summary: Let $X = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers and let $n \ge 0$. Then the partial placement sequence $P_n(X)$ is periodic: there is an integer $p > 0$ such that for every position $z \in \mathbb{Z}$, the positions $z + p$ and $z$ of $P_n(X)$ are either both empty or hold the same term.
nodes.title: Partial placement sequences are periodic

nodes.title: Recursive bound on the time to become leader

nodes.summary: Let $X = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct positive integers, and let $T(X) = (t_0, t_1, \dots)$ be its throwback sequence. Then every term $x_j$ of $X$ appears infinitely often in $T(X)$: there are infinitely many $k$ with $t_k = x_j$.
nodes.title: Every term recurs in the throwback sequence

nodes.summary: Let $X = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ be a sequence of pairwise distinct positive integers, and let $T(X) = (t_0, t_1, \dots)$ be its throwback sequence. Then for every $j$, the proportion $\#\{k < N : t_k = x_j\} / N$ of terms equal to $x_j$ among the first $N$ terms of $T(X)$ converges, as $N \to \infty$, to a nonzero real number.
nodes.title: Every term has a nonzero limiting frequency

nodes.title: Limiting frequencies in throwback sequences

nodes.summary: Let $X = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with throwback sequence $T(X) = (t_0, t_1, \dots)$. Then every block of consecutive terms of $T(X)$ recurs with bounded gaps: for all natural numbers $i$ and $L$ there is a natural number $G$ such that for every natural number $m$ there is an index $j$ with $m \le j \le m + G$ and $t_{j+s} = t_{i+s}$ for all $s < L$.
nodes.title: Throwback sequences of increasing sequences are uniformly recurrent

nodes.summary: For a sequence $X = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ of natural numbers, the throwback sequence $T(X) = (t_0, t_1, \dots)$ records the successive leaders under the throwback operation: $t_n$ is the leader (the entry at index $0$) of $\tau^n(X)$, where $\tau$ is the throwback operation in which each entry's weight is its own value.
nodes.title: Throwback sequence

nodes.summary: Let $s = (s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots)$ be a sequence of elements of a set $A$, each element $a$ carrying a weight $w(a) \in \mathbb{N}$. The throwback $\tau_w(s)$ moves the leader $s_0$ to index $w(s_0)$, moves the entries at indices $1, \dots, w(s_0)$ one place left and leaves later entries in place: $\tau_w(s)_i = s_{i+1}$ for $i < w(s_0)$, $\tau_w(s)_{w(s_0)} = s_0$, and $\tau_w(s)_i = s_i$ for $i > w(s_0)$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
